text:
Victor Eklund was the 16th pick in 2025, and history says players taken in that range score about a third of a point a game in their first full season. Eklund, 20, has 11 points in 20 games, seven of them goals, and the New York Times just put him on a list of eight rising players under 23. The New York Post wrote this week about Brayden Schenn taking him under his wing.

The numbers say to enjoy it with open eyes. He's shooting 23% against a league average of 13.4, and the Islanders have scored 10.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice. His own chances, 4.83 expected goals, are good for a rookie, but the goals have outrun them. At five-on-five the Isles get 47% of the expected goals with him out there, a bit worse than without him.

What doesn't regress is the work. He has 57 hits and 20 blocks, and Islanders reporter Stefen Rosner caught him blocking a point shot and then boxing out in front of Ilya Sorokin on the same sequence. That's a rookie earning trust, which matters more than the shooting percentage.
headline: Eklund is scoring before he's supposed to
